We already know how feckless Democratic Party leadership can be, and how
complicit it is in the US-Israeli war on Iran. Look no further than Senate
Minority Leader [Chuck
Schumer](https://x.com/SenSchumer/status/1929676991789203528?s=20), who
[responded](https://x.com/SenSchumer/status/2027765113617277225?s=20) by
fronting his concerns about how Donald Trump's "fitful cycles" put a wrench
into more "strategic" ways to confront Iran's "malign regional activities" and
"nuclear ambitions."

While House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries joined Schumer in calling on
Congress to vote for a War Powers Resolution to require congressional approval
for any military action in Iran, Jeffries didn't do much better in the
[throat-clearing
department](https://x.com/RepJeffries/status/2027751907754725757?s=20).

But what about the Democrats likely running for president in 2028? We've
collected their responses to Trump's illegal and dangerous war, and ranked
them here.

Without further ado - here is The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly:

# **The Good**

**Ro Khanna:**

Khanna, the California congressman, is one of the few Democrats actually using
his power to check Trump by leading a War Powers Resolution in the House. He
acknowledged the 93 million people in Iran and
[called](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DVTPyzJiHac/) the US-Israel assault
on the Islamic Republic what it is: "an illegal regime change war" that
endangers Americans.

**Ruben Gallego:**

The Arizona Senator delivered a [crisp
message](https://x.com/RubenGallego/status/2027776353827951054?s=20) befitting
of the moment and its contradictions: "Trump ran on exposing the pedophiles
and stopping wars. Trump is now protecting the pedophiles and starting wars."

**Chris Van Hollen:**

Van Hollen is among the few to condemn the killings of innocent Iranian
people, as hawks claim this war is being fought _for_ their freedom. "Trump is
lying to the American people as he launches an illegal, regime-change war
against Iran," the**** Maryland senator
[wrote](https://x.com/ChrisVanHollen/status/2027751753005817981). "This is
endangering American lives & has already resulted in mass civilian
casualties."

**Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez:**

Ocasio-Cortez checked Trump's fake rationale for the war,
[saying](https://ocasio-cortez.house.gov/media/press-releases/ocasio-cortez-
statement-trumps-combat-operations-iran) this was "not an inevitability," but
a "deliberate choice of aggression" by Trump, who "walked away" from
negotiating. "Violence begets violence. We learned this lesson in Iraq. We
learned this lesson in Afghanistan. And we are about to learn it again in
Iran," the New York congresswoman said.

**Pete Buttigieg:**

Buttigieg condemned Trump's "war of choice" for risking American lives,
ignoring US law, and endangering allies. "It does nothing to help with the
urgent problems here at home that Americans face every day," the former
transportation secretary
[said](https://x.com/PeteButtigieg/status/2027777322699440142).

**Jon Ossoff:**

While couching in "Iran's support for terrorism and uranium enrichment" as
destabilizing the region, Ossoff condemned Trump's lies about Iran posing a
threat, and his earlier contradictory claims that he "obliterated" Iran's
nuclear facilities. The Georgia senator, who's up for reelection this year,
[pushed](https://www.ossoff.senate.gov/press-releases/sen-ossoff-statement-on-
iran/) for an immediate vote on a War Powers resolution to stop Trump.

**JB Pritzker:**

Pritzker, the Illinois governor, slammed Trump for his expressed indifference
for US soldiers who may die from his war. "Donald Trump is once again
sidestepping the Constitution and once again failing to explain why he's
taking us into another war," Pritzker
[said](https://x.com/GovPritzker/status/2027754224814080325). "Americans asked
for affordable housing and healthcare, not another potentially endless
conflict."

**Kamala Harris:**

While Trump and his MAGA allies argued in 2024 that electing Kamala Harris
would mean a war in Iran, or World War III, the former vice president
condemned Trump's war. "Donald Trump is dragging the United States into a war
the American people do not want. Let me be clear: I am opposed to a regime-
change war in Iran, and our troops are being put in harm's way for the sake of
Trump's war of choice," she
[said](https://x.com/KamalaHarris/status/2027820065886777456?s=20).

# **The Bad**

**Gavin Newsom:**

The potential 2028 hopeful and part-time podcast bro criticized Trump's
"illegal, dangerous war." But Newsom, the California governor, led with
Trump's rationale,
[writing](https://x.com/CAgovernor/status/2027777089643151661): "The corrupt
and repressive Iranian regime must never have nuclear weapons. The leadership
of Iran must go."

**Cory Booker:**

Booker, a pro-Israel hawk who sits on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee,
[questioned](https://www.booker.senate.gov/news/press/booker-statement-on-
trumps-military-strikes-on-iran) Trump's strategy and acknowledged that the
president doesn't have "the authority to unilaterally wage war." He also
repeatedly warned about the threat of a nuclear-armed Iran and added:
"Military action **alone** cannot solve Iran's nuclear challenge."

**Wes Moore:**

The Maryland governor
[noted](https://x.com/GovWesMoore/status/2027840736758993398) "We can stand
with the Iranian people who support the cause of democracy and freedom without
risking another conflict that sends another generation of American troops into
combat." He did not mention the illegality of Trump's war, nor did he outright
oppose it.

**Andy Beshear:**

While the Kentucky governor dinged Trump for his hypocrisy for claiming he
would oppose new wars and noted that Americans are still dealing with the
fallout from US wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, he did not specifically oppose
the war. Beshear instead
[criticized](https://x.com/AndyBeshearKY/status/2027766822003482864) Trump for
not making the case for the war at his State of the Union - which implies
Trump's illegal war could be justified.

**Josh Shapiro:**

While the Pennsylvania governor expressed
[disappointment](https://x.com/GovernorShapiro/status/2027839394372001890)
that Trump has not "adequately explained" his war in Iran and launched it
without congressional approval, he still parroted neoconservative talking
points. The Iranian regime "is the leading state sponsor of terrorism around
the world - they must never be allowed to possess nuclear weapons," Shapiro
said.

# The Ugly

**Mark Kelly:**

The senator and the Navy combat veteran whom Trump's Justice Department tried
to prosecute with zero basis - offered some praise for Trump's illegal war and
the US-Israeli assassination spree in Iran. "I mean, it's a good thing that
the Supreme Leader is gone and some of the folks around him," the potential
2028 aspirant said, while critiquing Trump's lack of a plan.

Kelly tripped up when he was asked whether he would support a War Powers
resolution to block military action in Iran, saying that was "rather
unlikely." He quickly buckled under public pressure and said he will
[support](https://x.com/SenMarkKelly/status/2028166627015934025?s=20) it.

* * *

Just two days into Trump's war, voters are seeing who is a credible counter-
weight to the violent lawlessness of the out-of-control Republican Party and
who is not. But the stakes are not just an election two years from now.

The people are widely against this violence. Democratic leadership clearly
isn't up to snuff to channel that public will. Who will? And what will they do
_before_ 2028 to stop this?
